macro_context.market_sentiment: Strongly bullish — S&P 500 closed at record 7,365 (+1.46%) and Nasdaq at 25,839 (+2.02%) on May 6, with S&P futures continuing higher on May 7. AI-driven earnings beats and Iran peace deal hopes are propelling indices to new all-time highs.
macro_context.fed_outlook: Fed held rates at 3.5%–3.75% on April 29, 2026 (likely Powell's final meeting as Chair) amid unusual 8-4 dissent. Inflation remains elevated partly due to global energy prices from the Iran War. Markets are pricing zero rate cuts for the rest of 2026, with one 25bp cut not expected until December 2027.
macro_context.geopolitical: The ongoing Iran War is the dominant geopolitical risk — disrupting Strait of Hormuz shipping and energy supply, pushing global inflation. IMF forecasts 3.1% global growth and 4.4% inflation for 2026. Recent U.S.-Iran peace deal signals are the main driver of the current market rally, though the conflict remains unresolved.
key_events: U.S.-Iran peace negotiations progressing — White House close to a one-page MOU; resolution could cut energy prices and boost equities broadly
Nvidia Q1 2026 earnings due May 20 after close — AI bellwether widely watched
Fed leadership transition: Powell's successor appointment expected soon
U.S. tariff policy remains in flux — pressure on global trade and corporate margins

ticker_news.headline: Meta to cut ~8,000 jobs (10% of workforce) beginning May 20, restructuring into AI-focused 'pods' under new Chief AI Officer Alexandr Wang's Superintelligence Labs
Meta-backed Scale AI wins $500M U.S. Defense Department contract, 5x increase from prior $100M deal
Meta Q1 2026 EPS of $7.31 beat estimates of $6.67 by 9.6%; revenue growth of 33% YoY; capex guidance raised to $115–135B for 2026
Motley Fool: 'Troubling trend' in Meta Platforms has persisted for 3 straight quarters despite impressive revenue growth
Meta using AI profiling to infer user age and automatically enforce teen account restrictions across platforms

analyst_consensus.recent_changes: JP Morgan downgraded META to Neutral on April 30, 2026, cutting price target from $825 to $725 (citing elevated capex). Rosenblatt issued a $1,015 high target on April 30. Rothschild & Co upgraded to Buy with $900 target in January 2026. Consensus from 36–38 analysts: Strong Buy, avg PT $836–$839, range $700–$1,015. 31 buys, 7 holds, 0 sells.

competitor_activity: Meta is on track to surpass Google in global digital ad revenue for the first time in 2026 ($243B vs $239B projected). YouTube Shorts now reaches 2B+ monthly logged-in users, exceeding TikTok. Snap remains structurally weak — Meta's Q1 2026 ad revenue alone exceeded Snap's projected next 4 years combined. Antitrust scrutiny of Meta's social media dominance is intensifying. Smaller platforms (Snap, Pinterest) most exposed to ad budget cuts during geopolitical uncertainty, while spending concentrates on Meta and Google.
earnings_info: Q1 2026 reported April 29, 2026: EPS $7.31 (beat $6.67 est by 9.6%), revenue strong with 33% YoY growth. Next earnings: Q2 2026, expected July 29, 2026 after market close. Q2 2026 consensus estimates: EPS $7.19, revenue ~$60.17B.
